name: Saturn
fact: Saturn's density is 0.687 g/cm³ — less than water. Its ring system spans 282,000 km but is only tens of metres thick.
bio: The least dense planet — it would float on water. The ring system spans 282,000 km but is only metres thick. The 26.73° tilt means Earth sees the rings at different angles across Saturn's 29-year orbit.

science_sections.why: Saturn's 26.7° tilt is what makes its rings appear to open and close over the 29-year orbit — and what gives the planet hemispheric seasons that last more than seven Earth years.
Saturn has ~274 confirmed moons — the most of any planet — with Titan large enough to have its own dense atmosphere and Enceladus actively venting water from a subsurface ocean.
Cassini's 13-year orbital campaign was built around Kepler's laws — every ring-crossing and moon flyby was a Keplerian arc designed years in advance.
Saturn's orbit is gentle (eccentricity 0.054) but its 9.6 AU mean distance means perihelion and aphelion differ by 100 million km — Cassini timed its arrival to use the inbound speed.
